Adding the same constant to every $w_i$ leaves all cells and all volume constraints $|\mathscr{L}_i| = v_i$ unchanged, so the weights are determined only up to a common additive constant. diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then let $\mathscr{S}\subset\Omega$ be any shape of volume $v_i$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts $U(0) = 0$, which requires the zero level set $\{x : c(x,\bm{x}_i) = 0\}$ to have Lebesgue measure zero. For a general nonnegative cost this can fail (e.g., a cost with a flat zero region of positive measure would give $U(0) > 0$ and no $w^*$ with $U(w^*) = v_i$ for small $v_i$). The proof also claims a unique $w^*$ exists without proving existence (via continuity of $U$) or uniqueness (which requires level sets of $c$ to have measure zero). The lemma is stated for an unrestricted cost function, but the proof silently assumes these properties.

failure_location.quote: since the function $U : w \mapsto |\mathscr{S}(w)|$ is non-decreasing, $U(0)=0$ and $U(w)\to1$ as $w\to+\infty$ there exists a unique $w^*>0$ such that $U(w^*) = v_i$

issues.overall_effect: The lemma is unproved for general cost functions. For the specific costs used in the paper (power costs $|\bm{x}-\bm{x}_i|^\alpha$ with $\alpha > 0$) the zero level set is a single point and the argument is valid, so the numerical results are not affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the cell-doublet system of Lemma~\ref{lemma:celldoublet}, there are two triple junction points and $\bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{ijk}=0$ when the contact angle satisfies Young-Dupr\'e equation.

issues.failure_explanation: The total force at the triple junction is $\bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{ijk} = \bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{ij} + \bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{jk} + \bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{ki}$, but the force transmitted to $\bm{x}_i$ uses only $\bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{ij}$. At the Young-Dupré equilibrium $\bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{ijk} = 0$, so the correct force vanishes; the paper's formula gives a nonzero force $\text{proj}(\bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{ij})$. Additionally, the double sum $\sum_j \sum_k$ counts each junction twice (once as $(j,k)$ and once as $(k,j)$) with different incorrect vectors, so the total junction force is not a consistent approximation to $\text{proj}(\bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{ijk})$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{ij}$ with $\bm{\vec{\gamma}}_{ijk}$ in the force formula and restrict the dynamical sum to unordered pairs $(j,k)$ (or divide by 2) to avoid double-counting each junction.
issues.overall_effect: The cell-sorting dynamics (internalization, checkerboard, separation) is driven by an incorrect junction force that does not vanish at the Young-Dupré equilibrium. The stated sorting conditions in the figure caption are unreliable, and the claim that the model correctly implements the DITH is undermined.
issues.title: Triple junction force uses single interface tension instead of total junction tension
issues.why_classification: The repair is local (change one vector and adjust the summation) but alters the dynamics; the numerical sorting experiments must be re-run and re-validated, and the stated sorting regime conditions may change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The orange cells are internalized inside the mass of blue cells.

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated parameters $\gamma_{bw} - \gamma_{ow} = 7 - 30 = -23$, so the condition $\gamma_{bo} < -23$ is not satisfied by $\gamma_{bo} = 5 > 0$. The simulation shows orange engulfed by blue (as confirmed by the video description). The correct DITH condition for orange engulfed by blue (when $\gamma_{ow} > \gamma_{bw}$) is $\gamma_{bo} < \gamma_{ow} - \gamma_{bw} = 23$, which is satisfied. The paper's condition is the one for blue engulfed by orange (the opposite regime) and is wrong for the presented parameters and phenomenon.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\gamma_{bw} - \gamma_{ow}$ with $|\gamma_{bw} - \gamma_{ow}|$ (covering both engulfment directions) or with $\gamma_{ow} - \gamma_{bw}$ (matching the presented scenario).
issues.overall_effect: The stated condition for internalization is false for the given parameters and describes the wrong direction of engulfment. A reader applying this condition to other parameter regimes would obtain incorrect predictions.
issues.title: Internalization condition has wrong sign and is not satisfied by the stated parameters
issues.why_classification: The correction is a forced local change to one formula in a caption; the sorting pattern results themselves are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We also assume that the cost is of the form $c(\bm{x},\bm{y}) = \ell(\bm{y}-\bm{x})$ for a convex function $\ell$.
the Monge problem $T\# f = \mathrm{Leb}$ has a unique solution which is of the form $T(\bm{x}) = \bm{x} - (\nabla\ell)^{-1}(\nabla\Phi(\bm{x}))$

issues.failure_explanation: The transport cost $\mathcal{T}_c(\mu) = W_c(\mathrm{Leb},\mu)$ from the main text transports from Leb to $\mu$, so its first variation with respect to $\mu$ is the target Kantorovich potential $\psi_{LF}$. The derivation instead computes $\Phi$ from the reversed problem $T\#f = \mathrm{Leb}$ (transport from $f$ to Leb), where $\Phi$ is the source potential $\phi_{FL}$. These two potentials coincide only when $c(x,y) = c(y,x)$ (i.e., $\ell$ is even). For the stated class of general convex $\ell$ (which includes non-even functions), $\psi_{LF} \neq \phi_{FL}$ and the Fokker-Planck-Monge-Ampere system of Eq. (fpma) is derived from an incorrect drift term.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the derivation to even convex $\ell$ (symmetric costs) where the two potentials coincide, or redo the identification using the target potential $\psi_{LF}$ from the Leb-to-$f$ dual for general convex $\ell$.
issues.overall_effect: The Fokker-Planck-Monge-Ampere system in Eq. (fpma) is incorrect for non-symmetric costs allowed by the stated hypothesis. For symmetric costs (which include all costs used in the numerical experiments) the system is valid.
issues.title: Mean-field derivation identifies first variation with the wrong Kantorovich potential for non-symmetric costs
issues.why_classification: Restricting to symmetric costs is a limited weakening that preserves all numerical results and the PDE system in its practically relevant regime; alternatively, a contained re-derivation with the correct potential would be needed for full generality.
